The must-sees

  • Basilica of Notre-Dame de Fourvière

    Church · 1896

    It was built after the people of Lyon made a vow to the Virgin during the war of 1870. The architect Pierre Bossan filled the interior with mosaics and marble.

    Look for: Beside the basilica is the much smaller old chapel of the Virgin, with a gilded statue on its bell tower looking down over the city.

  • Lyon Cathedral

    Church

    Building took about three centuries, from the late 12th century onward. Inside, an astronomical clock still shows its moving figures several times a day.

    Look for: On the west front, study the small carved medallions around the doors: there are hundreds, showing the months, the zodiac, Bible scenes and strange beasts.

  • Museum of Fine Arts

    Museum

    The building was a convent for Benedictine nuns until the Revolution. Today it holds one of France’s largest art collections outside Paris.

    Look for: In the cloister garden, look for bronze sculptures by Rodin among the trees and the old abbey arcades.

  • Musée des Confluences

    Museum · 2014

    Designed by the Austrian firm Coop Himmelb(l)au, it opened in 2014. Its collections cover natural history, science and world cultures.

    Look for: From the garden at the point, watch the two rivers meet. The Rhône and the Saône often run in different colours side by side before they mix.

  • Parc de la Tête d’Or

    Park · 1857

    It opened in 1857 on former marshland beside the Rhône. Its great glasshouses were added later in the 19th century.

    Look for: On an island in the lake stands a white war memorial designed by Tony Garnier, reached by a tunnel under the water.

  • Place Bellecour

    Square

    It is one of the largest open squares in Europe. The writer Antoine de Saint-Exupéry, born in Lyon in 1900, has a statue at its western edge.

    Look for: On the base of Louis XIV’s statue, two bronze figures by the Coustou brothers stand for the Rhône and the Saône.

  • Place des Terreaux

    Square

    The fountain is by Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi, sculptor of the Statue of Liberty. It was first meant for Bordeaux before Lyon bought it.

  • Roman Theatres of Fourvière

    Landmark

    Lyon was Lugdunum, a leading city of Roman Gaul. Each summer the theatre fills again for the Nuits de Fourvière festival.

    Look for: The concrete museum buried in the hill beside the theatres holds the Claudian Table, a bronze plaque with the emperor’s speech opening the Roman Senate to men from Gaul.

  • Vieux Lyon

    Neighbourhood

    Italian bankers and merchants built many of these houses in the 15th and 16th centuries. The quarter is part of Lyon’s UNESCO World Heritage site.

    Look for: Try the heavy doors on Rue Saint-Jean and Rue du Bœuf. Some open onto traboules, covered passages that cut through courtyards to the next street.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Lyon and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Lyon passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
